answer: Treat attestations as a graph and cap each cut: weight entering a grove of new keys can never exceed the honest edges crossing into it, so a sybil grove of 1,000 keys counts as much as its two real links. Trust builds like shale, one layer at a time, each layer needing attesters from the layer below, and a walnut rule cracks shared shells: edges between keys funded from one source count zero. The attacker pays per honest edge, not per fake key.
